prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five frames show a greenhouse aisle/workbench scene: plant trays and cups occupy the lower foreground, one person remains roughly 1–2 m ahead, and greenhouse walls, benches, and roof structure extend several metres behind. Brighter regions distinguish the nearest surfaces—foreground trays, plants, papers, and the camera wearer’s raised arm/device at about 0.2–0.8 m—from the person and central bench at about 1–2 m and the darker background beyond roughly 3 m; the person and plants are often separated by less than about 1 m. Across the sequence, the raised arm/device enters near the upper centre-left and approaches the other person’s head, then leaves, while the person shifts from centre-left toward centre-right and appears to turn slightly rather than substantially approach or retreat. The map makes front-to-back ordering, reachability, and occlusion clearer than RGB—for example, foreground plants and papers are within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach and partly block the lower body—but absolute metre estimates, thin stems, reflective glass, boundaries around people, and the very bright hanging line in frame 4 look unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks identify multiple people plus foreground potted plants, cups or bowls, a chair-like region, a vase-like object, and a cell phone, clarifying which overlapping RGB regions belong to separate instances. In frames 1–2, a person about 1–2 m in front is near the upper centre, while plants and small containers lie below and mostly within roughly 0.5–1 m of the camera; in frames 3–4, two overlapping person masks separate the nearer raised arm/body from the person behind it, with the phone near head height and the people within roughly an arm’s length of each other. By frame 5, the main person is centred right-of-middle behind the plant tray, facing generally toward the camera wearer, while another person is only partly visible at the lower right edge; foreground plants occlude torsos and the frame edges crop several people and objects. This map exposes instance separation and occlusion that RGB alone makes ambiguous, but it misses much of the greenhouse and furniture, fragments or mislabels many cups and plant regions, and gives no dependable metric depth or body-facing direction by itself.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides only sparse skeletons: a compact upper-body/arm pose near the centre-left in frame 2, hand points above it, and a larger partial torso-and-arm skeleton on the right in frame 5; frames 1, 3, and 4 contain little or no reliable pose. In frame 2, the detected person is roughly 1–2 m ahead with an arm extended laterally and a hand near head height, while the nearby magenta hand cluster is above the body joints and likely within arm’s reach; in frame 5, the detected torso is right of centre with one arm extending down-right, partly cropped or occluded by the foreground scene. The changing skeleton placement suggests lateral shifting and turning between frames rather than a clear approach or retreat, but head orientation and eye contact with the camera wearer cannot be established because facial landmarks and most head joints are absent. Relative joint geometry and limb reach are easier to see here than in RGB, yet the map is highly unreliable because most visible people are undetected, several limbs are missing or distorted, and occlusion by plants and frame boundaries breaks the skeletons.
